questions.title: Overpaid
questions.story_md:
Overpaid staff have something to hide.

Using a CTE for department averages, return **id**, **first_name**, **dept** and **salary** of employees paid **more than their own department's average**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH avgs AS (SELECT dept, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY dept) SELECT e.id, e.first_name, e.dept, e.salary FROM employees e JOIN avgs a ON a.dept = e.dept WHERE e.salary > a.avg_salary;

hints.text: WITH avgs AS (SELECT dept, AVG(salary) …) then JOIN it.

questions.title: Richest Zone
questions.story_md:
Hit the richest zone only.

Return **zone** and **total value** of the zone(s) with the **highest total item value**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: WITH z AS (SELECT zone, SUM(value) AS total FROM vault_items GROUP BY zone) SELECT zone, total FROM z WHERE total = (SELECT MAX(total) FROM z);

hints.text: Compute totals in a CTE, then compare to MAX over the CTE.

questions.title: Bleeding Accounts
questions.story_md:
Accounts losing money are about to panic.

Return **account_id**, **total deposits** and **total withdrawals** for accounts whose withdrawals are **greater than** their deposits (only consider accounts with transactions).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: WITH flows AS (SELECT account_id, SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'deposit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS deposits, SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'withdrawal' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS withdrawals FROM transactions GROUP BY account_id) SELECT account_id, deposits, withdrawals FROM flows WHERE withdrawals > deposits;

hints.text: One CTE with two conditional sums.

questions.title: Frozen Branches
questions.story_md:
A branch with many frozen accounts is under investigation.

Return **branch name** and **number of frozen accounts** for branches with **at least {n}** frozen accounts.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE branches (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, city TEXT, opened TEXT, floors INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH frozen AS (SELECT branch_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM accounts WHERE status = 'frozen' GROUP BY branch_id) SELECT b.name, f.n FROM frozen f JOIN branches b ON b.id = f.branch_id WHERE f.n >= {n};

hints.text: Count per branch in a CTE, then join to branches.

questions.title: Frequent Visitors
questions.story_md:
Some staff are in the vault far more than others.

Return **employee_id** and **number of log entries** for employees whose count is **above the average count** (average over employees that have at least one entry).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM vault_logs GROUP BY employee_id) SELECT employee_id, n FROM c WHERE n > (SELECT AVG(n) FROM c);

hints.text: A CTE can be used twice: once to filter, once for AVG.

questions.title: Drowning in Debt
questions.story_md:
Owners who owe much more than they have will cooperate.

Return **account id**, **balance** and **total loans** for accounts whose total loan amount is **more than {x} times** their balance.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE loans (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, rate REAL, status TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: WITH debt AS (SELECT account_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM loans GROUP BY account_id) SELECT a.id, a.balance, d.total FROM accounts a JOIN debt d ON d.account_id = a.id WHERE d.total > {x} * a.balance;

hints.text: Sum loans per account in a CTE.

questions.title: Two-Bag Job
questions.story_md:
You can carry two items if they weigh at most **{cap}** kg together.

For zone **{zone}**, return the **tags of every pair** of different items that fit. List each pair once, with the **lower item id first** (two columns: first tag, second tag).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT a.tag, b.tag FROM vault_items a JOIN vault_items b ON b.zone = a.zone AND a.id < b.id WHERE a.zone = {zone|sql} AND a.weight_kg + b.weight_kg <= {cap};

hints.text: Join the table to itself; a.id < b.id lists each pair once.

questions.title: Chain of Command
questions.story_md:
Every crew member reports to a boss (`boss_id`).

Return the **name** of each **{role}** and the **name of their boss** (skip members without a boss).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE crew (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, role TEXT, boss_id INTEGER, cut INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT c.name, b.name FROM crew c JOIN crew b ON b.id = c.boss_id WHERE c.role = {role|sql};

hints.text: Join crew to crew: boss.id = member.boss_id.

questions.title: Mutiny Risk
questions.story_md:
Members who take a bigger cut than their boss cause trouble.

Return **id**, **name** and **cut** of crew members whose cut is **greater than their boss's cut**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE crew (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, role TEXT, boss_id INTEGER, cut INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, c.cut FROM crew c JOIN crew b ON b.id = c.boss_id WHERE c.cut > b.cut;

hints.text: Compare columns from the two aliases.

questions.title: Partners in Crime
questions.story_md:
Two different employees in the same zone on the same day might be working together.

For zone **{zone}**, return **distinct pairs of employee ids** (smaller id first) that both have a log entry there on the same day.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.employee_id, b.employee_id FROM vault_logs a JOIN vault_logs b ON b.zone = a.zone AND b.at = a.at AND a.employee_id < b.employee_id WHERE a.zone = {zone|sql};

hints.text: Self-join on zone and date; a.employee_id < b.employee_id.

questions.title: Department Heads
questions.story_md:
The best-paid person in each department holds the keys.

Return **dept**, **first_name** and **salary** of employees whose salary equals the **maximum in their own department** (ties: return all).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT e.dept, e.first_name, e.salary FROM employees e WHERE e.salary = (SELECT MAX(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.dept = e.dept);

hints.text: The subquery refers to the outer row: WHERE e2.dept = e.dept.

questions.title: Local Rich
questions.story_md:
Rich *for their branch*.

Return **id**, **branch_id** and **balance** of accounts whose balance is **above the average balance of their own branch**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT a.id, a.branch_id, a.balance FROM accounts a WHERE a.balance > (SELECT AVG(a2.balance) FROM accounts a2 WHERE a2.branch_id = a.branch_id);

hints.text: Correlate on branch_id.

questions.title: Last Move
questions.story_md:
Know each target's latest move.

For every account with transactions, return its **latest transaction**: **account_id**, **transaction id** and **at**. Latest = most recent date; if several on that date, the **highest id**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT t.account_id, t.id, t.at FROM transactions t WHERE t.id = (SELECT t2.id FROM transactions t2 WHERE t2.account_id = t.account_id ORDER BY t2.at DESC, t2.id DESC LIMIT 1);

hints.text: A correlated subquery can ORDER BY … LIMIT 1.
Compare ids, not dates, to break ties.

questions.title: Regulars Inside
questions.story_md:
Frequent vault users are easier to impersonate.

Return **id** and **first_name** of employees with **more than {n}** vault log entries, using a correlated COUNT.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT e.id, e.first_name FROM employees e WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vault_logs l WHERE l.employee_id = e.id) > {n};

hints.text: (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM … WHERE l.employee_id = e.id) > n

questions.title: First Alarm
questions.story_md:
The first alarm in each zone shows when security went live.

Return **zone**, **id** and **triggered** of the **earliest alarm in each zone** (if several on that date, the lowest id).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT a.zone, a.id, a.triggered FROM alarms a WHERE a.id = (SELECT a2.id FROM alarms a2 WHERE a2.zone = a.zone ORDER BY a2.triggered, a2.id LIMIT 1);

hints.text: Pick one id per zone with ORDER BY … LIMIT 1 in the subquery.

questions.title: Pecking Order
questions.story_md:
Rank people inside each department.

Return **id**, **dept**, **salary** and their **RANK** within the department by salary (highest = 1; equal salaries share a rank).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, dept, salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) FROM employees;

hints.text: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY … ORDER BY … DESC)

questions.title: Numbered Ledger
questions.story_md:
Number the moves of account **{account}**.

Return **transaction id**, **at** and a **sequence number** (1 = oldest; same date → lower id first).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY at, id) FROM transactions WHERE account_id = {account};

hints.text: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY at, id)

questions.title: Price Tags
questions.story_md:
Rank the items in zone **{zone}** by value, no gaps.

Return **tag**, **value** and **DENSE_RANK** by value (highest = 1).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT tag, value, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY value DESC) FROM vault_items WHERE zone = {zone|sql};

hints.text: DENSE_RANK leaves no gaps after ties.

questions.title: Branch League
questions.story_md:
Rank branches by money held.

Return **branch_id**, **total balance** and its **RANK** among branches (largest total = 1).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT branch_id, SUM(balance), RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(balance) DESC) FROM accounts GROUP BY branch_id;

hints.text: Window functions run after GROUP BY, so you can rank SUM(balance).

questions.title: Quartiles
questions.story_md:
Split targets into four groups.

Return **id**, **balance** and a **quartile** 1–4 using NTILE(4) over accounts ordered by **balance descending, then id**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, balance, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY balance DESC, id) FROM accounts;

hints.text: NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY …)

questions.title: First Visit
questions.story_md:
Everyone's first trip to the vault.

Return **employee_id**, **zone** and **at** of each employee's **first** log entry (earliest date, then lowest id).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT employee_id, zone, at FROM (SELECT employee_id, zone, at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY at, id) AS rn FROM vault_logs) WHERE rn = 1;

hints.text: Number rows per employee, keep rn = 1.

questions.title: Quiet Periods
questions.story_md:
Long gaps between alarms in zone **{zone}** are your window.

For each alarm in that zone (ordered by **triggered, then id**), return **id**, **triggered** and the **days since the previous alarm** (whole number; NULL for the first).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, triggered, CAST(julianday(triggered) - julianday(LAG(triggered) OVER (ORDER BY triggered, id)) AS INTEGER) FROM alarms WHERE zone = {zone|sql};

hints.text: LAG(triggered) OVER (ORDER BY triggered, id)
julianday difference gives days.

questions.title: Spending Jumps
questions.story_md:
Sudden jumps give people away.

For account **{account}**, return **transaction id**, **amount** and the **change from the previous transaction's amount** (ordered by at, then id; NULL for the first).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, amount, amount - LAG(amount) OVER (ORDER BY at, id) FROM transactions WHERE account_id = {account};

hints.text: amount - LAG(amount) OVER (…)

questions.title: Next Shift
questions.story_md:
Plan around employee **{emp}**'s schedule.

Return each of their shifts' **day**, **shift** and the **day of their next shift** (ordered by day, then id; NULL after the last).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE shifts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, day TEXT, shift TEXT, hours INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT day, shift, LEAD(day) OVER (ORDER BY day, id) FROM shifts WHERE employee_id = {emp};

hints.text: LEAD looks at the following row.

questions.title: Who Came Before
questions.story_md:
Each new hire was trained by the previous one.

For the **{dept}** department, return **first_name**, **hired** and the **first_name of the previous hire in that department** (by hired date, then id; NULL for the first).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT first_name, hired, LAG(first_name) OVER (ORDER BY hired, id) FROM employees WHERE dept = {dept|sql};

hints.text: Filter the department, then LAG over hire order.

questions.title: Running Tally
questions.story_md:
Track deposits into account **{account}** over time.

Return **id**, **at**, **amount** and the **running total** of deposit amounts (ordered by at, then id).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, at, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY at, id) FROM transactions WHERE account_id = {account} AND kind = 'deposit';

hints.text: SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY at, id)

questions.title: Alarm Counter
questions.story_md:
Each zone's alarm counter over the year.

Return **id**, **zone**, **triggered** and the **number of alarms so far in that zone** including this one (ordered by triggered, then id within the zone).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, zone, triggered, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY zone ORDER BY triggered, id) FROM alarms;

hints.text: COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY zone ORDER BY …)

questions.title: Smoothed Spending
questions.story_md:
Smooth out account **{account}**'s spending.

Return **id**, **amount** and the **average of this and the 2 previous transactions' amounts**, rounded to 2 decimals (ordered by at, then id; fewer rows at the start).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, amount, ROUND(AVG(amount) OVER (ORDER BY at, id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) FROM transactions WHERE account_id = {account};

hints.text: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW

questions.title: Grab Order
questions.story_md:
Grab the most valuable items first.

For zone **{zone}**, return **tag**, **value** and the **cumulative percentage of the zone's total value** after taking this item, rounded to 2 decimals (order by value descending, then id).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT tag, value, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(value) OVER (ORDER BY value DESC, id) / SUM(value) OVER (), 2) FROM vault_items WHERE zone = {zone|sql};

hints.text: SUM(value) OVER () is the whole total.
Divide the running sum by it.

questions.title: Year to Date
questions.story_md:
Track how much **{kind}** money moved through the bank.

Return **month** (`YYYY-MM`), that **month's total** and the **year-to-date total**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', at) AS month, SUM(amount) AS total FROM transactions WHERE kind = {kind|sql} GROUP BY month) SELECT month, total, SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY month) FROM m;

hints.text: Aggregate per month first, then a running SUM over months.
